card.band: 8 h. The four formats are independent buckets. xlsx and ods are easy, while BIFF8 xls with its CFB container, SST continuation records and xlsb record parsing are the long tail. A frontier agent usually finishes xlsx, ods and xlsb and gets part of xls. A weaker model stops after xlsx.
card.cheat: Shelling out to a Rust or Python library is blocked: there is no network and no such binary in the image, and the verifier runs pure Go in a clean container. Hidden workbooks are generated at grade time, so fixture-hardcoding fails.
card.grading: The repo's own fixtures (about 150 test files) plus workbooks made by a hidden generator (random types, shared strings, date systems, formulas, merged ranges). Output is compared exactly to JSON from the Rust reference binary, which is not in the image. Credit is per format and per case.
card.reference: Upstream Rust crate at the pinned tag, driven by a thin JSON-dump binary. The expected outputs are produced from it, and a faithful port scores 1 on the cases it passes.
card.task: /app ships a history-less Go module skeleton, a Rust-generated JSON dump schema and the sample workbooks. The agent ports the xlsx, xlsb, xls (BIFF/CFB) and ods readers to Go: sheet listing, cell values, dates, formulas, merged cells, errors. Delivery is a Go package plus a CLI that dumps a workbook to JSON.

spike_plan.kill_if: Dump is non-deterministic, the xls formula output is too shallow to score, or the fixture count per format is too small to give partial-credit buckets.
spike_plan.pass_if: Dump is deterministic across two runs, all four formats produce JSON on fixtures, and the xls bucket is reasonably sized relative to the others.
steps: In a throwaway Linux container with network, clone tafia/calamine at v0.37.0 and confirm commit f2c5948; run cargo test --offline --no-run on the smoke command (green in 17 s).
Build a small JSON-dump driver against the crate (open_workbook_auto, worksheets, cell values, formulas, merged ranges, errors) and dump about 30 fixtures spanning xlsx, xlsb, xls and ods.
Run the dump twice and diff the outputs to confirm determinism and that the schema pins number and date formatting.
Count how many of the fixtures are BIFF8 xls with SST continuation records or formulas; this sets the size of the xls bucket and tests whether the 0.9 threshold is reachable.
Reconcile the test count: smoke says tests_listed 284 but tests_total 217; list the test names to confirm which set the grader would use.

Check whether the Rust crate's xls formula decoding is fully implemented (decode a formula-bearing xls fixture); if it is partial, the reference score ceiling for xls drops and the scope should shrink.

v1.summary: The seed is a real, MIT-licensed, freshly pinned calamine v0.37.0 whose reference is public and whose smoke build is green, with a sealed generator and a strong Ref score. The main risk is Band: a 0.9-of-reference pass across four formats in 8 h, with the BIFF8 xls long tail, needs a spike before it is trusted, and the xls formula scope should be checked before launch.

v2.note: Real MIT repo, and the release and offline smoke build are confirmed. Four format buckets give natural credit. Gaps: (1) The Rust crate is only an oracle. The verifier needs a Go reference that scores 1, and writing that port plus a generator that writes BIFF8/CFB, xlsb and ods pushes build cost toward 5 days. (2) The MS-XLS, MS-XLSB and MS-CFB specs were not confirmed reachable; they must ship in /app or xls becomes recall-only. (3) The JSON schema must pin float and date formatting exactly, or valid ports fail on formatting rather than the work.
